title: Harmonize focus/hover blend for textfields to reduce visual jitter and preserve contrast
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: floating focus rings + hover surface tints on compact textfields are causing perceptible layout jitter at small sizes and failing contrast targets in high-contrast themes. We also have inconsistent uses of interaction tokens across platforms (web vs native) which complicates QA and causes regressions when token values change.

Goal: produce a single, token-driven interaction pattern that: (1) eliminates pixel-shift/jitter when focus or hover states change, (2) preserves WCAG AA contrast for both normal and compact density, and (3) is implementable by frontend engineers without per-component overrides. The deliverable will include token mappings, motion guidelines, a small set of CSS/JS examples, and a Figma component update with annotated specs for dev handoff.

Scope: text fields (single-line, multiline), selects (text-like triggers), and toggle-like inline inputs (clear, reveal). Excludes complex composite controls (autocomplete popovers) for this ticket — those will be follow-ups.

Constraints & trade-offs considered: maintaining a visible focus affordance for keyboard users vs minimizing layout shift for mouse users; preferring color+outline approach over box-shadow to reduce repaint cost on low-end GPUs; using token alpha blending for hover states to avoid adding extra DOM layers.
comments: 2025-01-10 — Aisha Patel: Created ticket after research spike; attached initial contrast matrix and screenshot samples from console QA. Observed 3ms layout shifts when toggling hover state on compact inputs (Chrome on macOS).

2025-01-11 — Marco Ruiz: Did on-device pass. Reproduced jitter in Safari/iOS; seems tied to using transform-based hint animations combined with outline change. Proposed switching to a static outline that animates opacity only. Added note to align with token interaction.focusRingAlpha.

2025-01-12 — Design Review: Reviewed with UX and Accessibility. Decision: focus indicator must be >= 3px thickness when in high-contrast mode and remain < 2px in compact density for visual balance; use an inner stroke (outline) instead of expanding box-shadow to avoid pushing layout. Action: create token mapping and two motion curves (keyboard and pointer).

2025-01-13 — Research: Ran A/B with 40 participants in prototype. Findings: opacity-based focus fade reduced perceived jitter by 86% and improved perceived responsiveness; however some keyboard users reported weaker affordance. This led to strengthening the focus ring alpha for keyboard interactions. Added microcopy hint for password inputs to ensure reveal control discoverability.

2025-01-14 — Eng sync: Spoke with ENG-22190 (runtime CSS infra). Agreed to expose two tokens: interaction.focus.strokeColor and interaction.hover.tintAlpha, with platform contract to avoid hard-coded colors. ENG requested CSS examples and a polyfill snippet for older browsers. Assigned small implementation PR.

2025-01-15 — PR: Marcos created draft PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/design-system/pull/482 — includes token updates, updated Figma components, and a CSS shim that animates opacity only. Need accessibility review before merge.

2025-01-16 — Accessibility Review (Lina Cho): Reviewed contrast table. Minor change: increase focus stroke alpha by 0.05 in high-contrast theme to reach 4.5:1 for small text. Also called out the need to keep :focus-visible behavior intact. Marked as required change.

2025-01-17 — QA: Added test plan to ticket — keyboard tab order, focus-visible tests on VoiceOver/JAWS, visual regression screenshots across densities and themes. Edge case: disabled fields should not receive animated transitions. QA notes linked in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/design/forms/focus-hover-blend.

2025-01-18 — Follow-ups noted: (1) Autocomplete popovers need variant token mapping (separate ticket), (2) Add unit tests in Storybook that assert no layout shift when toggling hover/focus for compact tokens, (3) Update iOS style guide for native mapping. Preparing final PR with accessibility fixes.
